title: Superannuation
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:12Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 may adapt ecb-superannuation, but is not highly sure, so to the Opus match check
2026-11-20T12:25:40Z confirm: Claude Opus 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

changes: Add that employers pay a set share of each employee's wages into the super fund, since the brief names this and the bank card does not mention it.
match.reason: The bank point teaches the same core idea of super as retirement savings at a suitable depth, but it does not mention employer payments from wages, which the brief requires.

confirm.reason: The new point defines super through employers paying a share of wages into a fund. The closest bank point, ecb-superannuation, defines super but never says who pays in, while the employer payment rule sits in a separate point (the superannuation guarantee), so no single bank point teaches this idea as briefed.

draft.title: Superannuation
card: Superannuation, or super, is money saved to live on in retirement. It is built up over a person's working life.
Employers pay super into a super fund for each eligible employee. The payment is a share of the employee's wages.
The fund holds and invests the money for the employee. The employee can usually only take it out when they reach retirement age, which is set by law.
Because the money is paid on top of wages and grows over many years, it can build a large amount by retirement.
draft.remember: Super is retirement savings that an employer pays into a fund as a share of wages.

a.q: Who pays the regular super contributions for an employee?
opts: The employer, into the employee's super fund
The employee, from their own pay each week
The bank, into the employee's savings account
The fund, into the employer's business account
a.why: Employers must pay super for eligible employees into a super fund. The money does not go into a savings account or to the employer, so those options are wrong.
a.clue: Think about who pays the wages.

b.q: Priya works part time at a bakery in Newcastle. Her boss pays a share of her wages into a fund she can usually only access in retirement. What is this payment?
b.why: Money paid by an employer into a fund as a share of wages, to be used in retirement, is superannuation. A loan is borrowed money that must be repaid, so it does not fit.
b.clue: Which one is saved for retirement?

a.best: The employer, into the employee's super fund
